items.title: Scammers Are Faking Official-Looking Notices — Here's the Tell
items.summary:
Scammers Are Faking Official-Looking Notices — Here's the Tell.

You get an email or see a webpage that looks exactly like it's from
your bank, the IRS, or a government agency. The logo is perfect.
The formatting is perfect. It says "Immediate action required" and
threatens account closure, legal trouble, or lost benefits if you
don't respond today.

The giveaway: they ask for something no legitimate organization
would ever request by email. Your Social Security number. Your
bank login. A payment in gift cards or wire transfer. Remote access
to your computer.

Real banks and government agencies don't operate this way. They
already have your information. They don't threaten instant disaster.
They don't demand gift cards.

What to do: Don't click any links in the message. Don't call...

items.title: Fake Windows update popup locks your screen — Microsoft never puts a phone number in an error
items.summary: That "Critical Windows Update" popup with a 1-800 number is a scam. Microsoft never includes phone numbers in warnings. Close the browser tab (Ctrl+W). If it won't close, hold your power button for 15 seconds until the screen goes black, then turn it back on.

items.title: Windows File History backs up your files automatically — free built-in, just plug in a drive
items.summary: Open Settings > System > Storage > Advanced storage settings > Backup options. Turn on File History, plug in a USB drive, and pick it as your backup drive. Windows saves copies of your files every hour.

items.summary: Go to ollama.com and download the Windows installer. Press Start, type 'cmd', press Enter, then type: ollama run llama3.2. Your private AI chatbot runs locally with no account, no cloud, no subscription.

items.summary: Go to bitwarden.com and create a free account. Install the browser extension and phone app. Bitwarden fills your logins, generates strong passwords, and syncs across unlimited devices. Open source, independently audited.

items.title: Password Manager Breach — mSecure Users Told to Change All Passwords
items.summary:
Password manager mSecure just told all users to change every password stored in their vault — but won't say what actually happened. On November 3, mSeven Software emailed customers about "suspicious activity" and said to immediately change passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and remove passkeys. They didn't say when it happened, what was accessed, or if your data was stolen. Because the scope is unknown, assume the worst: change your most important passwords first (email, banking, work) through each service's official website. Use a different, strong password for each. Consider moving to a different password manager until mSecure explains what happened.

Source: Malwarebytes — November 4–6, 2026

items.title: **Headline:** CISA warns WordPress sites under active attack — plus Windows 11 24H2 Home/Pro no longer get security updates
items.summary: WordPress Core vulnerability is being exploited right now — update WordPress at wordpress.org or your hosting panel. Also: Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro reached end of updates October 13 — go to Settings > Windows Update and check for the 26H2 upgrade to stay protected.
